_about: Aeschylus in English, translator per title. Complete in two translators: E. H. Plumptre (verse; Tragedies and Fragments) and John Stuart Blackie (verse, 1850; Lyrical Dramas). Also E. D. A. Morshead (verse; House of Atreus 1881 and Four Plays), T. A. Buckley (prose, Bohn), Gilbert Murray (Agamemnon, rhyming verse; Gutenberg clears it as US PD; Murray d. 1957, not PD in life+70 countries). Publication years are given only where checked in the file; Murray's per-play years were not, so they are left out. Older translations from the wishlist added 2026-10-02 as raw IA OCR (translator per row). Perseus TEI English (section "perseus", fetched by pipeline/fetch_perseus.py): translations published in or before 1930; the TEI markup is Perseus Digital Library's, CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution + share-alike), recorded per file in the report.

aeschylus-morshead-four: Four Plays of Aeschylus: Suppliant Maidens, Persians, Seven against Thebes, Prometheus Bound

aeschylus-murray-agamemnon: The Agamemnon of Aeschylus, translated into English rhyming verse

aeschylus-way-1907-part2: Aeschylus in English Verse, Part II: Prometheus Bound, The Suppliant Maidens (London, 1907) (year from the title page, 'Macmillan ... 1907'; IA records 1906)

_excluded.pg7073: Specimens of Greek Tragedy (Goldwin Smith): excerpts from Aeschylus and Sophocles, not whole plays
_excluded.Herbert Weir Smyth, Loeb (1922-26): now held from Perseus: the seven plays (aeschylus-perseus-smyth-*), English only. Perseus's source lines mark these files '(Modernized by Perseus.)', so the spelling may not be Smyth's as printed
_excluded.G. M. Cookson, Aeschylus' Plays (Everyma: the only scan with text (aeschylusplays0000gmco) is a later Everyman printing whose introduction cites a 1936 book, so it carries post-1930 matter; not taken
